questions.q: What is the physical setting of the Morgan household in "Birth," and what time of day does the story begin?
questions.a: The Morgan household is at Number 12 Blaina Terrace, a narrow-staired, poorly furnished bedroom lit by an oil lamp, in the Welsh mining town of Blaenelly. The story begins near midnight. A wrong answer (e.g., daytime, hospital) shows the student cannot locate basic setting details from the text.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the atmosphere in the kitchen while Andrew waits differs from the atmosphere in the bedroom during the resuscitation.
questions.a: The kitchen atmosphere is still, quiet, and heavy with Andrew's brooding thoughts (tick-tock clock, rustle of cinder, Morgan's footsteps outside), while the bedroom atmosphere becomes frantic, messy, and urgent during resuscitation (splashing water, sweat, basins, towels, Andrew's desperate efforts). A wrong answer that describes both as "tense" misses the shift from internal stillness to external chaos.

questions.q: Identify three sensory details from the text that create the atmosphere of the night walk to the Morgan house, and explain what mood they establish.
questions.a: Details: "cool and deep with quiet mystery" (touch/sound), "night air was cool" (touch), "deep with quiet mystery" (sound/silence). These establish a mood of anticipation and isolation, mirroring Andrew's listlessness. A wrong answer listing only visual details ignores the multisensory construction of atmosphere.

questions.q: Analyze how the setting of the mining town (Blaenelly) and the Morgan home reflects the socioeconomic context of the characters and influences the story's events.
questions.a: The mining town setting implies a working-class community (Joe is a "burly driller," the house is "clean but poorly furnished"), which explains the reliance on a midwife, the lack of modern medical facilities, and the high stakes of the birth for a family married twenty years. The cramped, oil-lit bedroom intensifies the physical struggle. A wrong answer that treats setting as mere background misses its causal role in the medical crisis.

questions.q: Evaluate whether the atmosphere at the end of the story (Andrew walking with miners at dawn) resolves the tension built earlier. Justify with evidence.
questions.a: Yes, the dawn atmosphere resolves the tension: "It was quite light. Nearly five o'clock. A few miners were already in the streets... his footfalls echoing with the others under the morning sky" contrasts with the opening "cool and deep with quiet mystery." The shared rhythm with miners and his thought "I've done something real at last" shows integration and purpose. A wrong answer claiming unresolved tension ignores the textual shift from isolation to community.

questions.q: Write a short paragraph (4-5 lines) describing a different setting for the same childbirth crisis (e.g., a modern hospital) and explain how the atmosphere would change.
questions.a: A strong answer would contrast the sterile, brightly lit, equipment-filled hospital with the dim, cramped bedroom, noting how the atmosphere shifts from raw, visceral struggle to clinical efficiency, potentially reducing the emotional intensity and Andrew's personal agency. A weak answer merely lists hospital features without linking to atmosphere change.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Setting refers to the time, place, and social ______ in which a story occurs, while atmosphere is the emotional tone or mood created through sensory details, descriptive language, and narrative pacing.
Fill in the blank: Imagine walking through an unfamiliar neighborhood at ______ — what do you notice?
What is Setting? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Setting refers to the time, place, and social environment in which a story occurs, while atmosphere is the emotional tone or mood created through sensory details, descriptive language, and narrative pacing.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: In "Birth," Andrew Manson experiences this as he walks to Number ______ Blaina Terrace.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify specific setting details (time, place, physical/social environment) and analyze how sensory language constructs atmosphere, using textual evidence to explain how setting-atmosphere interaction reflects character psychology and thematic concerns in "Birth.".
